chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah the Exalted did not grant Satan authority over those who have faith.
But [He granted authority] over those who take him as their guardian and disobey His command.

key_terms.يَتَوَلَّوْنَهُمْ: Those who take him as guardian/ally

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for Satan having authority over believers according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s (peace be upon him) clarification that Satan’s *sultan* (authority/power) is not inherent or absolute but contingent upon human voluntary submission (*ittiba'*). This hadith establishes the Shia theological principle of *Ikhtiyar* (free will), distinguishing between the general dominion of Satan over all humanity and his specific authority over those who consciously choose to follow his whispers, thereby affirming human agency in spiritual ascent or descent.
